name: GitHub Actions
what_it_is: GitHub's native event-driven CI/CD platform with hosted Linux, Windows, and macOS runners plus self-hosted runner support.
open_source: partial (actions/runner is MIT; GitHub Actions control plane is proprietary)
programmable_control: Start: `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches` or `gh workflow run <workflow> --ref <branch>`; Check: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}`, `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/check-runs`, or `gh run view <id> --json status,conclusion` / `gh pr checks <pr> --watch`; Stop: `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/cancel` or `gh run cancel <id>`. Docs: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs
auth_method: GitHub PAT (fine-grained or classic), GitHub App installation token, OAuth (`gh auth login`), or workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN`
usage_or_limits: REST API: `GET /organizations/{org}/settings/billing/actions`, `GET /users/{username}/settings/billing/actions`, `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/settings/billing/actions`, plus shared storage endpoint `/settings/billing/shared-storage`. Docs: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/billing/billing
pricing_model: Freemium; public repos free; private repos get 2,000 Linux min/mo and 500 MB storage free; Team $4/user/mo (3,000 min), Enterprise $21/user/mo (50,000 min); overage $0.006/min Linux 2-core, $0.010/min Windows, $0.062/min macOS
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64), Windows (x64, ARM64), macOS (Apple Silicon); self-hosted on any OS
fit_reason: Dominant checks provider with first-class `gh` CLI and REST API for checks, logs, rerun, cancel, and billing; already OpenWiz's primary CI integration.

name: GitLab CI/CD
what_it_is: GitLab's integrated CI/CD engine with SaaS shared runners and unlimited self-hosted runners across GitLab.com and self-managed instances.
open_source: partial (GitLab CE and gitlab-runner are MIT; Enterprise Edition is proprietary)
programmable_control: Start: `POST /api/v4/projects/{id}/pipeline` (`ref`, `variables`) or `glab ci run`; Check: `GET /api/v4/projects/{id}/pipelines/{pipeline_id}`, `GET /api/v4/projects/{id}/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/jobs`, or `glab ci status` / `glab ci view`; Stop: `POST /api/v4/projects/{id}/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/cancel` or `glab ci cancel`. Docs: https://docs.gitlab.com/api/pipelines/
auth_method: Personal/Project/Group Access Token (`PRIVATE-TOKEN` header), OAuth 2.0, `CI_JOB_TOKEN`, or `glab auth login`
usage_or_limits: REST API `GET /api/v4/groups/{id}/statistics` and GraphQL namespace billing fields for shared compute minutes and add-on packs. Docs: https://docs.gitlab.com/api/groups/
pricing_model: Freemium; Free tier $0 (5 users/group, 400 compute min/mo); Premium $29/user/mo (10,000 min/mo); Ultimate custom (50,000 min/mo); extra minutes $10/1,000 min; self-hosted runners free and unlimited
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64), Windows, macOS, Docker, Kubernetes; self-hosted on any OS
fit_reason: Second-largest forge-native CI with clean REST/GraphQL APIs, official `glab` CLI, commit status checks, and massive enterprise and self-hosted footprint.

name: Bitbucket Pipelines
what_it_is: Atlassian's built-in Docker-based CI/CD service inside Bitbucket Cloud with hosted and self-hosted runners.
programmable_control: Start: `POST /2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/`; Check: `GET /2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/{pipeline_uuid}` and `/steps/`; Stop: `POST /2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/{pipeline_uuid}/stopPipeline`. Docs: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-pipelines/
auth_method: Repository/Workspace/Project Access Token, Bitbucket API Token (Basic Auth), or OAuth 2.0
usage_or_limits: REST API: `GET /2.0/workspaces/{workspace}/pipelines-config/limits` and pipeline duration metrics on `/pipelines`. Docs: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-pipelines/
pricing_model: Freemium; Free tier $0 (50 build min/mo); Standard $3.65/user/mo (2,500 pooled min/mo); Premium $8.00/user/mo (3,500 pooled min/mo); overage $0.010/min; self-hosted runner slots $15/mo
os_platforms: Linux (Docker containers on x64/ARM64); self-hosted runners on Linux, macOS, Windows
fit_reason: Clean REST API for start, status, steps, stop, and minute limits; unlocks teams hosted on Bitbucket Cloud.

name: Azure Pipelines
what_it_is: Microsoft's cloud and on-premises CI/CD service in Azure DevOps with Microsoft-hosted and self-hosted agent pools.
open_source: partial (microsoft/azure-pipelines-agent is MIT; Azure Pipelines service is proprietary)
programmable_control: Start: `POST https://dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_apis/pipelines/{pipelineId}/runs?api-version=7.1` or `az pipelines run --id <id>`; Check: `GET .../_apis/pipelines/{pipelineId}/runs/{runId}` or `az pipelines runs show --id <runId>`; Stop: `PATCH .../_apis/build/builds/{buildId}?api-version=7.1` (`status: cancelling`) or `az pipelines build cancel --build-id <id>`. Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/azure/devops/pipelines/
auth_method: Personal Access Token (PAT), Microsoft Entra ID (OAuth 2.0), or `az login`
usage_or_limits: REST API: `GET https://dev.azure.com/{org}/_apis/distributedtask/resourceusage` for parallel job/minute quotas. Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/azure/devops/distributedtask/
pricing_model: Freemium; public projects get free unlimited parallel jobs; private projects get 1 free Microsoft-hosted job (1,800 min/mo) + 1 free self-hosted job; extra Microsoft-hosted parallel job $40/mo (unlimited min); extra self-hosted job $15/mo
os_platforms: Linux, Windows, macOS (hosted and self-hosted agents)
fit_reason: Enterprise mainstay with strong REST API and `az pipelines` CLI, plus generous concurrency-based pricing for heavy agent fleets.

name: CircleCI
what_it_is: High-parallelism SaaS and self-hosted CI/CD platform with reusable Orbs, test splitting, and Linux/Windows/macOS/GPU resource classes.
open_source: partial (circleci-cli is MIT; CircleCI platform and Server are proprietary)
programmable_control: Start: `POST /api/v2/project/{project-slug}/pipeline` (and API v3 pipeline trigger endpoints); Check: `GET /api/v2/pipeline/{pipeline-id}/workflow` and `GET /api/v2/workflow/{id}/job`; Stop: `POST /api/v2/workflow/{id}/cancel` or `POST /api/v2/project/{project-slug}/job/{job-number}/cancel`; CLI: `circleci config validate`, `circleci local execute`. Docs: https://circleci.com/docs/api/v2/index.html
auth_method: Personal or Project API Token (`Circle-Token` header) or OAuth
usage_or_limits: Insights & Usage API: `POST /api/v2/organizations/{org_id}/usage_export_job` and `GET /api/v2/insights/{project-slug}/workflows` for credit consumption and job metrics. Docs: https://circleci.com/docs/api/v2/index.html#tag/Usage
pricing_model: Freemium credit-based; Free $0/mo (30,000 credits/mo ≈ 3,000 Linux Medium min, up to 5 users); Performance from $15/mo + $0.0006/credit ($15 per 25k credit pack); Scale custom; self-hosted Server custom
os_platforms: Linux (Docker, VM x64/ARM64, GPU), Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon); self-hosted runners
fit_reason: Mature REST API v2/v3 with clean pipeline trigger, workflow/job status, cancel, and usage export endpoints, widely used alongside GitHub repos.

name: Buildkite
what_it_is: Hybrid CI/CD platform pairing a fast hosted control plane with self-hosted or Buildkite-hosted agents and dynamic pipeline uploads.
open_source: partial (buildkite/agent and cli are MIT; Buildkite control plane is proprietary)
programmable_control: Start: `POST /v2/organizations/{org}/pipelines/{pipeline}/builds` or `bk build new`; Check: `GET /v2/organizations/{org}/pipelines/{pipeline}/builds/{number}` or `bk build view`; Stop: `PUT /v2/organizations/{org}/pipelines/{pipeline}/builds/{number}/cancel` or `bk build cancel`; also GraphQL API. Docs: https://buildkite.com/docs/apis/rest-api/builds
auth_method: API Access Token (Bearer token), GraphQL token, or `bk configure`
usage_or_limits: REST/GraphQL agent & job queues API (`GET /v2/organizations/{org}/agents`, GraphQL `organization.usage` unverified for self-serve billing totals; rate-limit headers `RateLimit-Remaining`). Docs: https://buildkite.com/docs/apis/rest-api
pricing_model: Freemium seat + compute; Free tier up to 5 users; Pro $30/active user/mo (unlimited build minutes on self-hosted agents, 4,000 Linux vCPU-min hosted included, 10 agents, $3.50/extra agent/mo); Enterprise custom
os_platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows, FreeBSD, Kubernetes, Elastic CI Stack for AWS/GCP
fit_reason: Best-in-class REST + GraphQL APIs and `bk` CLI for dynamic pipelines, massive monorepos, and private-cloud agent fleets.

name: Semaphore
what_it_is: Fast cloud and self-hosted CI/CD platform positioned for modern and agent-heavy workflows with per-minute compute billing.
open_source: partial (Semaphore CE open-sourced under Apache-2.0; Semaphore Cloud is proprietary)
programmable_control: Start: `POST /api/v1alpha/plumber-workflows` or `sem` CLI (`sem attach`, `sem create`); Check: `GET /api/v1alpha/pipelines/{pipeline_id}` or `sem get workflows` / `sem get pipelines`; Stop: `PATCH /api/v1alpha/pipelines/{pipeline_id}` (`terminate_request: true`) or `sem stop pipeline <id>`. Docs: https://docs.semaphoreci.com/reference/api-v1alpha/
auth_method: API Token (`Authorization: Token <token>`) and `sem connect <org> <token>`
usage_or_limits: Billing & usage API / org dashboard (`sem` CLI and billing endpoints; exact public self-serve billing endpoint unverified). Docs: https://docs.semaphoreci.com/reference/api-v1alpha/
pricing_model: Usage-based with free monthly credit (~$15/mo free credits ≈ 2,000 Ubuntu x64 2-vCPU min, 20 concurrent jobs); Ubuntu x64 $0.0075/min (2-vCPU), ARM $0.003/min, macOS $0.09/min; self-hosted agents $0.0025/min
os_platforms: Linux (Ubuntu x64, ARM64), macOS, Docker, Kubernetes; self-hosted agents
fit_reason: Clean `sem` CLI and REST API with open-source CE option and strong agent-workflow positioning.

name: Travis CI
what_it_is: Long-running hosted and enterprise CI/CD service supporting Linux, Windows, macOS, and FreeBSD builds.
open_source: partial (travis-build and CLI are MIT; hosted platform is proprietary)
programmable_control: Start: `POST https://api.travis-ci.com/repo/{repo}/requests`; Check: `GET https://api.travis-ci.com/build/{build.id}` or `travis status` / `travis show`; Stop: `POST https://api.travis-ci.com/build/{build.id}/cancel` or `travis cancel <build>`. Docs: https://docs.travis-ci.com/api/
auth_method: Travis API Token (`Authorization: token <token>`, header `Travis-API-Version: 3`) or `travis login`
usage_or_limits: REST API v3: `GET /allowance/by_owner/{owner}` and `GET /v3/owner/{login}/executions` for credit usage. Docs: https://docs.travis-ci.com/api/
pricing_model: Subscription + credit-based; trial credits (10,000 credits) and validated OSS credits available; paid plans from ~$13.75-$15+/mo; Travis CI Enterprise custom
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64, s390x, ppc64le), Windows, macOS, FreeBSD
fit_reason: Complete REST API v3 and Ruby CLI, though mindshare has declined heavily in favor of GitHub Actions and modern runner clouds.

name: TeamCity
what_it_is: JetBrains' full-featured CI/CD server (on-premises and TeamCity Cloud) with Kotlin DSL pipelines, build chains, and test intelligence.
programmable_control: Start: `POST /app/rest/buildQueue` (XML/JSON build payload); Check: `GET /app/rest/builds/id:{buildId}` and `/app/rest/buildQueue`; Stop: `POST /app/rest/builds/id:{buildId}` (`buildCancelRequest`). Docs: https://www.jetbrains.com/help/teamcity/rest-api.html
auth_method: Bearer Access Token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) or HTTP Basic Auth
usage_or_limits: REST API: `GET /app/rest/server/licensingData` and agent/build statistics endpoints (`/app/rest/builds/{locator}/statistics`). Docs: https://www.jetbrains.com/help/teamcity/rest-api.html
pricing_model: Freemium on-prem (TeamCity Professional free forever with 3 build agents and 100 configs); Enterprise Server $2,399/yr (3 agents) + $359/agent/yr; TeamCity Cloud from $45/mo (3 committers, 24,000 credits) + $15/committer/mo
os_platforms: Linux, Windows, macOS, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS/Azure/GCP cloud agents
fit_reason: Very rich REST API and strong enterprise/game-dev/JVM adoption, with both free on-prem Professional tier and managed Cloud.

name: Harness CI
what_it_is: Enterprise CI module within the Harness software delivery platform with hosted cloud runners, Test Intelligence, and Drone heritage.
open_source: partial (Harness Open Source / Gitness is Apache-2.0; Harness CI SaaS/Enterprise is proprietary)
programmable_control: Start: `POST /pipeline/api/pipeline/execute/{identifier}` or `hc` / `harness` CLI; Check: `GET /pipeline/api/pipelines/execution/v2/{planExecutionId}`; Stop: `PUT /pipeline/api/pipelines/execution/interrupt/{planExecutionId}` (`interruptType=AbortAll`). Docs: https://apidocs.harness.io/
auth_method: Harness API Key (`x-api-key` header) / Personal or Service Account Token
usage_or_limits: Harness Platform API exposes license and subscription utilization endpoints (`/gateway/ng/api/licenses/account/summary`). Docs: https://apidocs.harness.io/
pricing_model: Freemium; Free tier up to 5 developers with limited monthly build minutes; Essentials and Enterprise custom quote based on seats and Harness Cloud build minutes
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64), Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon), Kubernetes, Docker
fit_reason: Full REST API for execution, polling, abort, and license usage; strong enterprise penetration especially among former Drone and webapp.io shops.

name: RWX
what_it_is: Content-addressed, cloud-native CI/CD platform with persistent cloud sandboxes, per-second billing, Captain test analytics, and an MCP server.
open_source: partial (rwx CLI and Captain CLI are open source / MIT; RWX Cloud platform is proprietary)
programmable_control: Start: `rwx run <file> --init ...` or `rwx sandbox`; Check: `rwx runs`, `rwx logs`, `rwx artifacts`, and hosted RWX MCP server for agent querying; Stop: CLI/run cancellation (exact REST cancel endpoint unverified). Also official Terraform provider `rwx-cloud/rwx`. Docs: https://www.rwx.com/docs/rwx/cli
auth_method: CLI device login (`rwx login`) or `$RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN` / `--access-token`
usage_or_limits: CLI command `rwx billing` reports current monthly usage and billing metrics directly from the terminal. Docs: https://www.rwx.com/docs/rwx/cli
pricing_model: Usage-based per-second billing (~$0.00007/sec/vCPU, 100 GB cache, unlimited parallelism/users); free OSS tier and $100 trial credits; Captain test analytics $10/million results; Enterprise custom
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64); CLI on macOS, Linux, Windows/WSL
fit_reason: Built explicitly for agentic loops with content-addressed caching, `rwx` CLI, `rwx billing`, cloud sandboxes, and native MCP server.

name: Depot CI
what_it_is: High-speed CI platform, BuildKit container builder, GitHub Actions runner cloud, and ephemeral sandbox service with per-second billing.
open_source: partial (depot CLI and Node/Go SDKs are MIT; Depot Cloud platform is proprietary)
programmable_control: Start/Check/Stop: Connect RPC API (`https://api.depot.dev`, OpenAPI v3 + gRPC/HTTP-JSON) for Depot CI workflows (dispatch, rerun, list runs/jobs/attempts, logs, cancel), BuildKit builds, GHA runners, and Sandboxes; CLI: `depot ci run list`, `depot ci workflow list`, `depot ci diagnose --run <id>`, `depot build`. Docs: https://depot.dev/docs/api/overview
auth_method: Bearer token (`DEPOT_TOKEN`) or CLI OAuth login (`depot login`, `depot login token`)
usage_or_limits: Usage Analysis API (`api.depot.dev`) returns daily usage and resource breakdowns across projects, repos, and workflows. Docs: https://depot.dev/docs/api/overview
pricing_model: Subscription + metered overage; Developer $20/mo (2,000 GHA min, 2,000 Sandbox min, 500 Build min, 25 GB cache); Startup $200/mo (20k GHA, 20k Sandbox, 5k Build, 250 GB); overages $0.006/min GHA 2-vCPU, $0.00005/sec/vCPU CI/Sandbox; Business custom; no permanent free tier
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64), macOS runners; CLI on macOS, Linux, Windows
fit_reason: First-class Connect RPC API, `depot ci diagnose` for coding agents, Usage Analysis API, and dual support for standalone Depot CI plus GHA runner acceleration.

name: Buddy
what_it_is: Developer-friendly SaaS and self-hosted CI/CD platform with visual and YAML pipelines, isolated sandboxes, and fast caching.
programmable_control: Start: `POST https://api.buddy.works/workspaces/{domain}/projects/{project_name}/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/executions`; Check: `GET .../executions/{execution_id}`; Stop: `PATCH .../executions/{execution_id}` (`operation: CANCEL`). OpenAPI spec available. Docs: https://buddy.works/docs/api/getting-started/overview
auth_method: Personal Access Token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) or OAuth 2.0
usage_or_limits: REST API workspace/quota endpoints and response rate-limit headers (exact billing usage endpoint unverified). Docs: https://buddy.works/docs/api/getting-started/overview
pricing_model: Freemium; Free plan (1 seat, 2 concurrent pipelines, $1/mo usage credit); Pro $29/mo + $20/extra seat + pay-as-you-go compute; Team $299/mo (5 concurrent runs, SSO)
os_platforms: Linux (Docker containers on x64/ARM64); self-hosted Buddy On-Premises on Linux
fit_reason: Clean OpenAPI-backed REST API for starting, checking, and cancelling pipeline executions, though smaller market share in open-source fleets.

name: AppVeyor
what_it_is: Hosted and on-premises CI/CD service historically popular for Windows/.NET builds alongside Linux and macOS.
programmable_control: Start: `POST https://ci.appveyor.com/api/builds`; Check: `GET https://ci.appveyor.com/api/projects/{account}/{project}/build/{version}` and `/api/buildjobs/{jobId}/log`; Stop: `DELETE https://ci.appveyor.com/api/builds/{account}/{project}/{buildVersion}`. Docs: https://www.appveyor.com/docs/api/projects-builds/
auth_method: Bearer API Token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`)
usage_or_limits: none (no dedicated usage-quota REST endpoint documented; concurrency limits enforced per plan)
pricing_model: Free for open-source projects and free On-Premise Team Edition; Cloud private plans start at $29/mo (Basic), $59/mo (Pro), $99/mo (Premium); On-Premise Enterprise from $2,990/yr
os_platforms: Windows, Linux (Ubuntu), macOS
fit_reason: Simple REST API v2 with start, log, and cancel endpoints; useful mainly for legacy Windows/.NET repositories.

name: Codefresh
what_it_is: Kubernetes- and Argo-focused CI/CD and GitOps platform now operated by Octopus Deploy.
open_source: partial (Argo CD/Workflows/Rollouts are Apache-2.0; Codefresh platform is proprietary)
programmable_control: Start: `POST https://g.codefresh.io/api/pipelines/run/{id}` or `codefresh run <pipeline>`; Check: `GET https://g.codefresh.io/api/builds/{id}` or `codefresh get build <id>`; Stop: `DELETE https://g.codefresh.io/api/builds/{id}` or `codefresh terminate <id>`. Docs: https://codefresh.io/docs/integrations/codefresh-api/
auth_method: Codefresh API Key (`Authorization: <token>`) or `codefresh auth create-context`
usage_or_limits: none (usage tracked in platform UI; no public self-serve billing meter endpoint verified)
pricing_model: Enterprise/GitOps packaged tiers via Octopus Deploy (evaluation trials available; public GitOps Cloud entry from ~$4,170/yr for cluster/app packs)
os_platforms: Linux, Kubernetes (hybrid and cloud runtimes); CLI on macOS, Linux, Windows
fit_reason: Good CLI and REST API for container/GitOps pipelines, but increasingly enterprise GitOps-focused under Octopus Deploy.

name: CodeShip
what_it_is: Hosted CI service (Basic and Docker-based Pro) originally built by Codeship, later owned by CloudBees, and revived independently under Codeship Labs in 2026.
programmable_control: Start: `POST /v2/organizations/{org_uuid}/projects/{project_uuid}/builds`; Check: `GET /v2/organizations/{org_uuid}/projects/{project_uuid}/builds/{build_uuid}`; Stop: `POST .../builds/{build_uuid}/stop`; CLI `jet` for local Pro runs (2026 Codeship Labs API changes unverified). Docs: https://docs.cloudbees.com/docs/cloudbees-codeship/latest/api-overview
auth_method: API v2 JWT obtained via HTTP Basic Auth (`POST /v2/auth`)
usage_or_limits: none (unverified under 2026 Codeship Labs relaunch)
pricing_model: unverified (historically free tier with 100 builds/mo plus paid concurrency plans; 2026 Codeship Labs pricing unverified)
os_platforms: Linux (Docker / hosted VMs)
fit_reason: Legacy CI recently relaunched under Codeship Labs with unverified 2026 API/pricing stability.

name: Jog
what_it_is: Drop-in Linux x64 GitHub Actions runner cloud built for agent-scale CI with per-second billing, Zen 5 Max runners, and the Joggernaut agent plugin.
open_source: partial (usejog/joggernaut agent skill/plugin is open source; runner cloud is proprietary)
programmable_control: Controlled via GitHub Actions workflow runs (`runs-on: jog`, `jog-4vcpu`..`jog-32vcpu`, `jog-max-*`) using GitHub's REST API / `gh run` to start, check, and cancel jobs; Joggernaut plugin audits and migrates workflows via `gh`. No separate Jog REST control API documented. Docs: https://usejog.com/docs/runners/
auth_method: GitHub App installation (workflows authenticated via GitHub); Stripe prepaid account
usage_or_limits: none (no public Jog usage API documented; credit balance and per-second usage viewed in dashboard)
pricing_model: Prepaid per-second billing with 5,000 free min/mo (2-vCPU baseline) on paying accounts; Standard 2 vCPU $0.0012/min up to 32 vCPU $0.0176/min; Jog Max (Zen 5) 2x rate; no idle fees
os_platforms: Linux (Ubuntu x64)
fit_reason: Ultra-cheap drop-in GHA runner built explicitly for high-volume coding agent fleets; works transparently through OpenWiz's existing GitHub Actions checks provider.

name: Blacksmith
what_it_is: Bare-metal gaming-CPU and Firecracker microVM drop-in GitHub Actions runner cloud with sticky disks, flex scheduling, and Testboxes.
programmable_control: CI jobs started/checked/stopped through GitHub Actions (`runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404`, `;scheduling=flex`) via `gh` / GitHub REST API; `blacksmith` CLI inspects jobs/logs/caches and controls agent Testboxes (`blacksmith testbox warmup | run | status`). No public general-purpose REST API. Docs: https://docs.blacksmith.sh/
auth_method: GitHub App installation (`app.blacksmith.sh`) and CLI login
usage_or_limits: `blacksmith` CLI usage and cost reporting commands plus spend threshold alerts in dashboard. Docs: https://docs.blacksmith.sh/
pricing_model: Pay-as-you-go per-minute with 3,000 free runner min/mo and free cache storage allowance; ~33% cheaper per minute than GitHub-hosted runners; flex scheduling ~40% off
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64), Windows, macOS
fit_reason: Fast drop-in GHA runner with `blacksmith` CLI telemetry, 3,000 free min/mo, and agent Testboxes; plugs cleanly into OpenWiz via GitHub Actions + optional CLI diagnostics.

name: Namespace
what_it_is: Ephemeral cloud compute platform offering high-density GitHub Actions runners, remote Docker/Bazel builders, Devboxes, and an MCP server.
open_source: partial (namespacelabs/foundation and CLI tooling open source / Apache-2.0; Namespace Cloud is proprietary)
programmable_control: CI jobs via GitHub Actions labels or direct compute control via Protocol Buffers / gRPC / Connect API (`{region}.compute.namespaceapis.com`, `global.namespaceapis.com`, `buf.build/namespace/cloud`) and `nsc` / `devbox` CLIs (`nsc login`, `nsc bazel setup`, instance create/inspect/destroy). Docs: https://namespace.so/docs/reference/api
auth_method: CLI OAuth login (`nsc login`), tenant bearer tokens (`iam.namespaceapis.com`), or GitHub OIDC
usage_or_limits: Compute API (`{region}.compute.namespaceapis.com`) exposes instance usage metrics in compute-unit minutes (1 vCPU + 2 GB RAM for 1 min). Docs: https://namespace.so/docs/reference/api
pricing_model: Usage-based compute units with no seat charges; Developer pay-as-you-go, Team (~$100/mo), Business (~$250/mo) with included compute allocations, Enterprise custom; no permanent free tier verified
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64), macOS (Apple Silicon), Windows
fit_reason: Strongly typed Protobuf/Connect API + `nsc` CLI + MCP server covering both GHA runners and full ephemeral Devboxes (could also serve as a cloud driver).

name: WarpBuild
what_it_is: High-performance GitHub Actions runner platform supporting both managed cloud runners (Linux, Windows, Apple Silicon) and BYOC on AWS/GCP/Azure.
programmable_control: CI jobs controlled via GitHub Actions (`runs-on: warp-...`) using GitHub API / `gh`; WarpBuild Automation API and `wb` CLI manage custom VM images, snapshots, and macOS sandboxes. Docs: https://docs.warpbuild.com/
auth_method: GitHub App installation, WarpBuild API Key, and `wb` CLI login
usage_or_limits: Automation API / dashboard usage tracking (exact billing endpoint unverified). Docs: https://docs.warpbuild.com/
pricing_model: Pay-as-you-go per-minute; hosted Linux x64 $0.004/min (2 vCPU) to $0.064/min (32 vCPU), Apple Silicon M4/M5 Pro ~$0.08-$0.16/min; BYOC $0.002/min platform fee + your cloud compute; free trial credits available
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64), Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon M4/M5 Pro)
fit_reason: Covers both managed runners and BYOC across AWS/GCP/Azure plus Apple Silicon, working seamlessly behind GitHub Actions.

name: RunsOn
what_it_is: Self-hosted AWS EC2 orchestrator for ephemeral GitHub Actions runners with zero per-minute markup and S3 caching.
open_source: partial (CloudFormation/Terraform configs and `roc` CLI open; RunsOn server binary source-available/commercial license)
programmable_control: CI jobs controlled via GitHub Actions (`runs-on: runs-on=${{ github.run_id }}/runner=2cpu-linux-x64`) using `gh` / GitHub API; `roc` CLI manages local RunsOn config; public EC2 pricing API at `https://go.runs-on.com/api/`. Docs: https://runs-on.com/docs/
auth_method: GitHub App installed in your AWS account (IAM roles) + license key
usage_or_limits: AWS CloudWatch metrics and Cost Explorer in user's AWS account (no separate RunsOn metering API needed)
pricing_model: Flat annual license + raw AWS EC2 costs (zero markup; e.g. ~$0.0009/min Spot); free for OSS/non-profits; Starter €300/$350/yr (<50k jobs/mo), Growth €900/yr, Scale €1,800/yr, Enterprise €3,600/yr
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64), Windows, GPU instances on AWS EC2
fit_reason: Cheapest high-scale GitHub Actions option for teams with an AWS account; works transparently with OpenWiz's GitHub Actions checks.

name: Ubicloud Runners
what_it_is: Open-source cloud platform providing low-cost bare-metal-backed GitHub Actions runners on Hetzner/Leaseweb.
programmable_control: CI jobs controlled via GitHub Actions (`runs-on: ubicloud-standard-2`) using GitHub API / `gh`; Ubicloud REST API (`https://api.ubicloud.com`) and `ubi` CLI manage VMs, runners, and projects. Docs: https://www.ubicloud.com/docs/api
auth_method: Personal Access Token (Bearer) for REST API / `ubi` CLI + GitHub App for runners
usage_or_limits: REST API / dashboard billing and credit tracking (exact billing endpoint unverified). Docs: https://www.ubicloud.com/docs/api
pricing_model: Pay-as-you-go per-minute with $2.50/mo free runner credits (~1,250 min); Standard Linux x64 2 vCPU $0.00125/min, Premium $0.002/min; self-hostable for free (AGPL-3.0)
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64)
fit_reason: AGPL-3.0 open-source cloud with super cheap GHA runners and a clean REST API + `ubi` CLI.

name: Tenki
what_it_is: Single-tenant ephemeral VM GitHub Actions runner provider offering per-second Linux x64 and Apple Silicon macOS runners.
programmable_control: CI jobs controlled via GitHub Actions `runs-on` labels using GitHub API / `gh`; no public standalone Tenki REST API documented (unverified). Docs: https://tenki.cloud/
auth_method: GitHub App installation
usage_or_limits: none (unverified; metered per-second in dashboard)
pricing_model: Per-second core-minute billing with Starter sign-up credits; Linux x64 ~$0.002/vCPU-min, Apple Silicon macOS ~$0.020/vCPU-min, cache $0.20/GB-mo; Team plans from ~$200/mo
os_platforms: Linux (x64), macOS (Apple Silicon)
fit_reason: Competitive per-second Linux and Apple Silicon GHA runners, transparent behind GitHub Actions.

name: Sprinters
what_it_is: BYOC AWS EC2 GitHub Actions runner orchestrator charging a flat $0.01/job fee instead of per-minute markups.
open_source: no (proprietary orchestrator; runs in user's AWS account)
programmable_control: CI jobs controlled via GitHub Actions `runs-on` labels (specifying EC2 instance type/region) using GitHub API / `gh`; no separate REST control API needed. Docs: https://sprinters.sh/docs/
auth_method: GitHub App + AWS IAM role
usage_or_limits: AWS EC2 billing in user's account; Sprinters job count in dashboard (no public API verified)
pricing_model: Free for public repos; private repos $0.01/job flat fee (first 1,000 jobs free for 30 days) + raw AWS EC2 compute; no monthly base fee
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64), Windows, GPU on AWS EC2
fit_reason: Simple flat-per-job AWS BYOC runner that plugs in transparently via GitHub Actions.

name: Actuated
what_it_is: Firecracker microVM runner control plane for GitHub Actions and GitLab CI on your own bare-metal servers.
open_source: no (proprietary commercial software; CLI tools open on GitHub)
programmable_control: CI jobs controlled via GitHub Actions or GitLab CI APIs; `actuated-cli` inspects microVM logs, agent logs, server telemetry, and repairs agents (`actuated-cli logs`, `agent-logs`, `repair`). Docs: https://docs.actuated.com/
auth_method: GitHub App / GitLab token + `actuated-cli` OAuth/token
usage_or_limits: Prometheus metrics endpoint and `actuated-cli` telemetry for server/VM utilization. Docs: https://docs.actuated.com/
pricing_model: Flat per-server subscription (no free tier): $150/mo for first bare-metal server, $125/mo each additional server; unlimited build minutes and concurrency on your hardware
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64 bare-metal hosts running Firecracker microVMs)
fit_reason: Secure Firecracker microVM isolation for teams running GHA or GitLab CI on their own bare metal.

name: Northflank
what_it_is: Full-stack cloud and BYOC platform with native container CI build pipelines, jobs, and per-second self-hosted GitHub Actions runners.
programmable_control: Start: `POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/services/{serviceId}/build` or `POST .../jobs/{jobId}/runs`; Check: `GET .../builds/{buildId}` or `northflank list builds`; Stop: `DELETE .../builds/{buildId}` or job run cancel; official JS/Python SDKs and CLI. Docs: https://northflank.com/docs/v1/api
auth_method: API Token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) or `northflank login`
usage_or_limits: REST API billing/metrics endpoints for project compute and build usage. Docs: https://northflank.com/docs/v1/api
pricing_model: Per-second usage-based (Cloud or BYOC on AWS/GCP/Azure/Oracle/bare metal); compute from ~$0.01667/vCPU-hr; free developer sandbox tier available
os_platforms: Linux (Kubernetes containers, x64/ARM64, GPU)
fit_reason: Clean REST API, CLI, and JS/Python SDKs with BYOC per-second builds, though primarily an app/PaaS platform rather than a dedicated PR checks provider.

name: GitHub Actions Runner Controller (ARC)
what_it_is: Official Kubernetes operator that autoscales ephemeral self-hosted GitHub Actions runner scale sets on Kubernetes clusters.
programmable_control: CI jobs started/checked/stopped via GitHub Actions REST API / `gh run`; runner scale sets managed declaratively via Kubernetes CRDs (`AutoscalingRunnerSet`) and `kubectl` / Helm. Docs: https://github.com/actions/actions-runner-controller
auth_method: GitHub App or PAT stored in Kubernetes Secret + Kubernetes RBAC
usage_or_limits: Kubernetes Prometheus metrics (`gha_assigned_jobs`, `gha_running_jobs`, `gha_desired_runners`) via controller metrics endpoint
pricing_model: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); pay only for your Kubernetes cluster compute
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64), Windows containers on Kubernetes
fit_reason: Standard open-source Kubernetes autoscaler for self-hosted GitHub Actions; works transparently with OpenWiz's GitHub Actions integration.

name: Tart + Cilicon
what_it_is: Open-source Apple Silicon macOS VM toolchain (Tart) paired with ephemeral runner orchestrators (Cilicon, Tartelet, tartci) for self-hosted macOS CI.
open_source: yes (Tart: Fair Source 0.9 / Cirrus Labs; Cilicon: MIT)
programmable_control: CI jobs controlled via GitHub Actions / GitLab CI / Buildkite APIs; VMs controlled locally via `tart clone`, `tart run`, `tart exec`, `tart stop`, `tart delete` (OCI registry push/pull). Docs: https://tart.run/quick-start/
auth_method: OCI registry auth (`tart login`) + forge runner registration token
usage_or_limits: none (local/dedicated Mac hardware utilization only)
pricing_model: Free software (Tart Fair Source, Cilicon MIT); pay only for dedicated Mac hardware (e.g. OakHost, MacStadium, AWS EC2 Mac, or local Mac Studios)
os_platforms: macOS (Apple Silicon hosts running macOS and Linux ARM64 VMs)
fit_reason: Go-to self-hosted Apple Silicon CI stack after Cirrus Runners shut down; works behind GitHub Actions, GitLab, or Buildkite.

name: Jenkins
what_it_is: The ubiquitous open-source Java automation server with 1,900+ plugins, Groovy Jenkinsfiles, and distributed build agents.
programmable_control: Start: `POST /job/{name}/build` or `/buildWithParameters` (or `java -jar jenkins-cli.jar build <job>`); Check: `GET /job/{name}/{buildNumber}/api/json` and `/consoleText`; Stop: `POST /job/{name}/{buildNumber}/stop` or `/kill`. Docs: https://www.jenkins.io/doc/book/using/remote-access-api/
auth_method: HTTP Basic Auth with User API Token + CSRF crumb (`Jenkins-Crumb`)
usage_or_limits: REST API `/computer/api/json` and `/queue/api/json` expose executor counts, busy executors, and queue depth. Docs: https://www.jenkins.io/doc/book/using/remote-access-api/
pricing_model: Free and open source (MIT); self-hosted infrastructure costs only
os_platforms: Linux, Windows, macOS, Docker, Kubernetes (JVM controller + agents on any OS)
fit_reason: Still runs a massive share of enterprise CI; simple REST API for build trigger, status JSON, console log, and stop.

name: Jenkins X
what_it_is: Kubernetes-native GitOps CI/CD distribution built on Tekton, Lighthouse (ChatOps), and Helm.
programmable_control: Start: `jx pipeline start <pipeline>` or PR ChatOps (`/test`); Check: `jx get build logs`, `jx pipeline grid`, or Kubernetes Tekton `PipelineRun` API; Stop: `jx pipeline stop <pipeline>`. Docs: https://jenkins-x.io/v3/develop/reference/jx/
auth_method: Kubernetes kubeconfig + Git provider token
usage_or_limits: Kubernetes cluster resource quotas (`kubectl describe resourcequota`)
pricing_model: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); self-hosted on Kubernetes
os_platforms: Linux (Kubernetes)
fit_reason: Opinionated Kubernetes GitOps stack; OpenWiz is better off integrating Tekton directly than Jenkins X specifically.

name: Woodpecker CI
what_it_is: Lightweight, community-maintained, container-native open-source CI engine forked from Drone CI; powers Codeberg CI.
programmable_control: Start: `POST /api/repos/{repo_id}/pipelines` or `woodpecker-cli pipeline start`; Check: `GET /api/repos/{repo_id}/pipelines/{pipeline}` and `/logs/{step_id}` or `woodpecker-cli pipeline info`; Stop: `POST /api/repos/{repo_id}/pipelines/{pipeline}/cancel` or `woodpecker-cli pipeline stop`. OpenAPI spec included. Docs: https://woodpecker-ci.org/docs/usage/cli
auth_method: Personal Access Token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) or forge OAuth (GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo, Gitea, Bitbucket)
usage_or_limits: REST API `/api/queue/info` and `/api/agents` report queue stats and worker concurrency. Docs: https://woodpecker-ci.org/docs/administration/api
pricing_model: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); self-hosted (free hosted instance for OSS on Codeberg CI)
os_platforms: Linux, Windows, macOS (Docker, Kubernetes, or local execution backends)
fit_reason: Clean Apache-2.0 REST API + `woodpecker-cli` with multi-forge support (GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo, Gitea) and active community.

name: Drone CI
what_it_is: Container-native self-hosted CI engine acquired by Harness and largely succeeded in the community by Woodpecker CI and Harness Open Source.
open_source: partial (OSS/Community parts Apache-2.0; enterprise features proprietary commercial license)
programmable_control: Start: `POST /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/builds` or `drone build create`; Check: `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/builds/{build}` or `drone build info`; Stop: `DELETE /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/builds/{build}` or `drone build stop`. Docs: https://docs.drone.io/api/overview/
auth_method: Bearer API Token (`DRONE_TOKEN`) + `DRONE_SERVER`
usage_or_limits: REST API `GET /api/queue` for running/pending builds. Docs: https://docs.drone.io/api/overview/
pricing_model: Free Community/OSS edition (capped/limited enterprise features); commercial features folded into Harness CI
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64), Windows, macOS (Docker, Kubernetes, SSH, Exec runners)
fit_reason: Clean REST API and `drone` CLI, but corporate momentum shifted to Harness CI and community momentum shifted to Woodpecker CI.

name: Concourse CI
what_it_is: Declarative, container-native, resource-driven CI/CD engine controlled via the `fly` CLI with reproducible isolated tasks.
programmable_control: Start: `fly -t <target> trigger-job -j <pipeline>/<job>` or `POST /api/v1/teams/{team}/pipelines/{pipeline}/jobs/{job}/builds`; Check: `fly -t <target> builds` / `fly watch` or `GET /api/v1/builds/{build_id}`; Stop: `fly -t <target> abort-build -b <id>` or `PUT /api/v1/builds/{build_id}/abort`. Docs: https://concourse-ci.org/fly.html
auth_method: OAuth/OIDC/local login via `fly login` (Bearer JWT token)
usage_or_limits: CLI `fly workers` and API `GET /api/v1/workers` expose active container/volume counts and worker capacity. Docs: https://concourse-ci.org/fly.html
pricing_model: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); self-hosted
os_platforms: Linux (x64, ARM64), Windows, macOS workers; `fly` CLI on macOS, Linux, Windows
fit_reason: Rock-solid `fly` CLI and REST API for trigger, watch, and abort, though resource-based model requires more setup for standard PR checks.

name: GoCD
what_it_is: Open-source continuous delivery server specializing in complex value-stream maps, fan-in/fan-out pipelines, and deployment modeling.
programmable_control: Start: `POST /go/api/pipelines/{pipeline_name}/schedule`; Check: `GET /go/api/pipelines/{pipeline_name}/{counter}` and `/go/api/stages/{pipeline}/{counter}/{stage}/{stage_counter}`; Stop: `POST /go/api/stages/{pipeline}/{counter}/{stage}/{stage_counter}/cancel`. Docs: https://api.gocd.org/current/
auth_method: Personal Access Token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) or HTTP Basic Auth
usage_or_limits: REST API `GET /go/api/agents` exposes elastic and static agent capacity. Docs: https://api.gocd.org/current/
pricing_model: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); self-hosted
os_platforms: Linux, Windows, macOS, Docker, Kubernetes (JVM server + agents)
fit_reason: Well-documented REST API with schedule, status, and cancel endpoints, though more CD/value-stream oriented than PR-check oriented.

name: Buildbot
what_it_is: Python-based, highly programmable open-source continuous integration framework used by major open-source compilers and infrastructure projects.
programmable_control: Start: JSON-RPC `POST /api/v2/forceschedulers/{name}` (`method: force`); Check: REST `GET /api/v2/builds/{buildid}` and `/api/v2/builds/{buildid}/steps`; Stop: JSON-RPC `POST /api/v2/builds/{buildid}` (`method: stop`). Docs: https://docs.buildbot.net/current/developer/rest.html
auth_method: Session cookie, OAuth2, or HTTP Basic Auth (configurable per instance)
usage_or_limits: REST API `GET /api/v2/workers` and `/api/v2/buildrequests` for worker and queue state. Docs: https://docs.buildbot.net/current/developer/rest.html
pricing_model: Free and open source (GPL-2.0); self-hosted
os_platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows, FreeBSD, Solaris (any Python 3 platform)
fit_reason: Clean REST + JSON-RPC v2 API and deep adoption in systems projects (LLVM, Python, MariaDB), though self-hosted configuration varies per site.

name: Zuul
what_it_is: Project-gating CI/CD system famous for speculative cross-repository merge testing (used by OpenStack, Ansible, BMW, Volvo).
programmable_control: Start: `zuul enqueue` / `POST /api/tenant/{tenant}/project/{project}/enqueue` (or Gerrit/GitHub PR triggers); Check: `GET /api/tenant/{tenant}/status` and `GET /api/tenant/{tenant}/builds`; Stop: `zuul dequeue` / `POST /api/tenant/{tenant}/project/{project}/dequeue`. Docs: https://zuul-ci.org/docs/zuul/latest/rest-api.html
auth_method: OIDC / JWT Bearer token for admin REST API; public read-only status API on many instances
usage_or_limits: REST API `GET /api/tenant/{tenant}/nodes` (Nodepool worker capacity) and `/status`. Docs: https://zuul-ci.org/docs/zuul/latest/rest-api.html
pricing_model: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); self-hosted
os_platforms: Linux (Ansible-based job execution across clouds, OpenStack, AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, static nodes)
fit_reason: Unmatched speculative cross-repo gating with REST API and `zuul` CLI, though heavy to operate and niche outside OpenInfra/auto enterprises.

name: Gitea Actions
what_it_is: Built-in GitHub-Actions-compatible CI/CD engine inside the self-hosted Gitea Git forge, powered by `act_runner`.
programmable_control: Start: `POST /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow}/dispatches` or `gt` CLI; Check: `GET /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/tasks` and `/actions/runs/{run_id}`; Stop: run cancellation via Gitea Actions API (full parity evolving; exact cancel endpoint version-dependent). Docs: https://docs.gitea.com/api/1.22/
auth_method: Gitea Personal Access Token (`Authorization: token <token>`), OAuth2, or `gt` CLI login
usage_or_limits: REST API runner registration/list endpoints (`/api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runners`); self-hosted so no minute caps
pricing_model: Free and open source (MIT); self-hosted (Gitea Cloud commercial hosting also available)
os_platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows, Docker (`act_runner`)
fit_reason: GitHub Actions-compatible workflows and REST API make it easy to support alongside GitHub Actions for self-hosted Gitea users.

name: Forgejo Actions
what_it_is: Community-led, GPL-licensed GitHub-Actions-compatible CI/CD engine built into Forgejo (powering Codeberg and sovereign forges).
programmable_control: Start: `POST /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow}/dispatches` or community `fj`/`fgh` CLIs; Check: `GET /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/tasks` and `/actions/runs`; Stop: Actions API run cancellation (evolving per release). Docs: https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/user/actions/overview/
auth_method: Forgejo Access Token (`Authorization: token <token>`) or OAuth2
usage_or_limits: Self-hosted runner inventory via Forgejo API; no hosted minute caps on self-hosted instances
pricing_model: Free and open source (GPL-3.0-or-later); self-hosted or free for FOSS on Codeberg
os_platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows, Docker, LXC (`forgejo-runner`)
fit_reason: Fast-growing sovereign Git forge with GHA-compatible workflows and expanding Actions REST API.

name: SourceHut Builds
what_it_is: Minimalist, fast, QEMU/VM-based continuous integration service (`builds.sr.ht`) supporting Linux, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, and Alpine.
programmable_control: Start: GraphQL `submit` mutation (`https://builds.sr.ht/query`) or `hut builds submit <manifest.yml>`; Check: GraphQL `job(id: ...)` query or `hut builds show <id>` / `hut builds list`; Stop: GraphQL `cancel(jobId: ...)` mutation or `hut builds cancel <id>`. Docs: https://man.sr.ht/builds.sr.ht/graphql.md
auth_method: OAuth2 Personal Access Token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) or `hut init`
usage_or_limits: GraphQL API exposes user job history and concurrency limits (self-hosted has no caps). Docs: https://man.sr.ht/builds.sr.ht/graphql.md
pricing_model: Pay-what-you-can subscription for project hosts (€4/€8/€12/mo, identical features; contributors free; financial aid available); 100% free to self-host (AGPL-3.0)
os_platforms: Linux (Alpine, Arch, Debian, Fedora, NixOS, Ubuntu, etc.), FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, 9front
fit_reason: Super clean GraphQL API and `hut` CLI for submit/show/cancel, plus unmatched BSD and minimalist Linux VM coverage.

name: Tangled Spindles
what_it_is: Decoupled, self-hostable CI runner service (Spindles) for the AT Protocol-based federated Git forge Tangled, using `.tangled/workflows/`.
programmable_control: Triggered automatically via ATProto/knot git push events against `.tangled/workflows/`; programmatic trigger/cancel REST/XRPC endpoints are early/evolving (unverified). Docs: https://tangled.org/
auth_method: AT Protocol (DID / OAuth / App Passwords) and knot-spindle pairing
usage_or_limits: none (self-hosted spindle capacity)
pricing_model: Free and open source (MIT); self-hosted spindles (hosted Tangled community tiers evolving)
os_platforms: Linux (Nix, Docker, microVMs)
fit_reason: Exciting federated ATProto Git + Nix/microVM CI architecture, but still early-stage with evolving programmatic APIs.

name: OneDev
what_it_is: All-in-one self-hosted Git server, issue tracker, and container/K8s CI/CD engine with built-in symbol search and low resource footprint.
programmable_control: Start: `POST /~api/job-runs`; Check: `GET /~api/builds/{buildId}` and `/~api/builds/{buildId}/log`; Stop: `DELETE /~api/job-runs/{buildId}`. Docs: https://docs.onedev.io/category/restful-api
auth_method: HTTP Basic Auth or Personal Access Token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`)
usage_or_limits: REST API `/~api/agents` for connected build agent capacity
pricing_model: Free and open source (MIT); optional Enterprise subscription for HA/cluster features
os_platforms: Linux, Windows, macOS, Docker, Kubernetes
fit_reason: Clean REST API for running, checking, and cancelling builds, appealing to small self-hosted teams.

name: Vela
what_it_is: Container-native, Go-based pipeline automation framework built by Target for high-scale enterprise GitHub/GitLab CI.
programmable_control: Start: `POST /api/v1/repos/{org}/{repo}/builds` or `vela restart build`; Check: `GET /api/v1/repos/{org}/{repo}/builds/{build}` or `vela view build`; Stop: `DELETE /api/v1/repos/{org}/{repo}/builds/{build}/cancel` or `vela cancel build`. Docs: https://go-vela.github.io/docs/reference/api/
auth_method: Bearer Token (`VELA_TOKEN`) via OAuth with GitHub/GitLab or `vela login`
usage_or_limits: REST API `GET /api/v1/workers` and Prometheus metrics for worker/queue utilization. Docs: https://go-vela.github.io/docs/reference/api/
pricing_model: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); self-hosted
os_platforms: Linux (Docker, Kubernetes); CLI on macOS, Linux, Windows
fit_reason: Well-engineered Go REST API and `vela` CLI, though adoption is concentrated in self-hosted enterprise setups.

name: Agola
what_it_is: Open-source microservices CI/CD platform supporting Starlark/Jsonnet/YAML pipelines and direct local runs.
programmable_control: Start: `agola directrun start` or REST `POST /api/v1alpha/projects/{projectref}/runs`; Check: `GET /api/v1alpha/projects/{projectref}/runs/{runnumber}`; Stop: `POST /api/v1alpha/projects/{projectref}/runs/{runnumber}/actions` (`action_type: cancel`). Docs: https://agola.io/doc/
auth_method: Bearer API Token (`Authorization: token <token>`) or OAuth2 with GitHub/GitLab/Gitea
usage_or_limits: none (self-hosted executor capacity)
pricing_model: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); self-hosted
os_platforms: Linux (Docker, Kubernetes)
fit_reason: Interesting Starlark/Jsonnet pipeline model and REST API, but small community adoption.

name: Screwdriver.cd
what_it_is: Open-source continuous delivery platform built by Yahoo for high-scale microservices on Kubernetes and Docker.
programmable_control: Start: `POST /v4/events` (`pipelineId`, `startFrom`); Check: `GET /v4/builds/{id}` and `/v4/builds/{id}/steps/{name}/logs`; Stop: `PUT /v4/builds/{id}` (`status: ABORTED`). Docs: https://docs.screwdriver.cd/user-guide/api
auth_method: JWT Bearer Token (`POST /v4/auth/token` via API token or SCM OAuth)
usage_or_limits: REST API `/v4/pipelines/{id}/metrics` for build durations and queue times. Docs: https://docs.screwdriver.cd/user-guide/api
pricing_model: Free and open source (BSD-3-Clause); self-hosted
os_platforms: Linux (Kubernetes, Docker, Nomad)
fit_reason: Complete v4 REST API, but niche adoption outside Yahoo and a handful of large enterprises.

name: Laminar
what_it_is: Ultra-lightweight, fast C++ continuous integration server for Linux with no plugins and script-based jobs.
programmable_control: Start: `laminarc queue <job>` or `laminarc run <job>` (over Unix/TCP Cap'n Proto socket); Check: `laminarc show-running`, `laminarc show-queued`, or HTTP SSE stream; Stop: `laminarc abort <job> <run>`. Docs: https://laminar.ohwg.net/docs.html
auth_method: Unix socket permissions / SSH / network ACL (no built-in user auth)
usage_or_limits: CLI `laminarc show-jobs` / `show-running` / `show-queued` (configured executor slots)
pricing_model: Free and open source (GPL-3.0); self-hosted
os_platforms: Linux
fit_reason: Minimalist `laminarc` CLI control for queue/run/abort, but lacks built-in forge PR checks or multi-tenant auth.

name: Phorge Harbormaster
what_it_is: Build and CI orchestration module inside Phorge (the community fork of Phabricator) that tracks buildables and dispatches to external or Drydock builders.
programmable_control: Start/Check/Stop via Conduit RPC API: `harbormaster.queryautotargets`, `harbormaster.buildable.search`, `harbormaster.build.search`, `harbormaster.sendmessage` (`pass`/`fail`/`work`), and `arc` CLI. Docs: https://we.phorge.it/book/phorge/
auth_method: Conduit API Token (`api.token` parameter)
usage_or_limits: Conduit `drydock.resource.search` for Drydock lease/worker availability
pricing_model: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); self-hosted
os_platforms: Linux (PHP server; dispatches to any external CI or Drydock host)
fit_reason: Relevant only to teams running Phorge/Phabricator with Differential code reviews.

name: Dagger
what_it_is: Open-source, BuildKit-powered programmable CI/CD engine where pipelines are written in Go, TypeScript, or Python and run identically locally or in any CI.
open_source: yes (Apache-2.0 for Dagger Engine, CLI, and SDKs; Dagger Cloud is proprietary)
programmable_control: Start: `dagger call <function>` or `dagger check` (or GraphQL API / Go, TypeScript, Python SDKs); Check: streamed OpenTelemetry / Dagger Cloud trace UI and exit codes; Stop: SIGTERM/SIGINT on `dagger` process or context cancellation in SDK. Docs: https://docs.dagger.io/api/
auth_method: Local engine requires no auth; Dagger Cloud uses `dagger login` or `DAGGER_CLOUD_TOKEN`
usage_or_limits: Dagger Cloud telemetry/plan usage in web console (exact public billing API unverified); self-hosted engine has no limits
pricing_model: Core engine free and open source (Apache-2.0); Dagger Cloud has a free tier for individuals/OSS, Starter/Team plans (from ~$50/mo) with trace retention and native Git checks, Enterprise custom
os_platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows (via Docker/Podman/containerd/Kubernetes engine)
fit_reason: Portable Apache-2.0 `dagger call` / `dagger check` execution lets OpenWiz agents run the exact same CI pipeline locally and in cloud fleets with step-level caching.

name: Tekton Pipelines
what_it_is: Kubernetes-native open-source framework for defining cloud-native CI/CD pipelines as Kubernetes CRDs (`Task`, `Pipeline`, `PipelineRun`).
programmable_control: Start: `tkn pipeline start <name>` or `kubectl create` a `PipelineRun` CRD via Kubernetes API; Check: `tkn pipelinerun describe <run>` / `tkn pipelinerun logs <run>` or `GET /apis/tekton.dev/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pipelineruns/{name}`; Stop: `tkn pipelinerun cancel <run>` or patch `spec.status: Cancelled`. Docs: https://tekton.dev/docs/pipelines/pipelineruns/

name: Hydra
what_it_is: The NixOS Foundation's open-source Nix-based continuous build and binary-cache system powering Nixpkgs and NixOS.
programmable_control: Start: `POST /api/push?jobsets={project}:{jobset}` (evaluates jobset); Check: `GET /build/{id}` (`Accept: application/json`) and `/jobset/{project}/{jobset}/evals`; Stop: `POST /api/cancel-build` / admin endpoint (session-authenticated). Docs: https://github.com/NixOS/hydra
auth_method: Session cookie login (`POST /login`) for mutating endpoints; public read-only JSON on public instances
usage_or_limits: JSON endpoints `/queue-runner-status` and `/machines` expose build queue and remote builder capacity
pricing_model: Free and open source (GPL-3.0); self-hosted
os_platforms: Linux, macOS (Nix remote builders)
fit_reason: Essential for NixOS/Nixpkgs ecosystems, though clunky cookie-auth JSON API compared to modern forges.

name: Mozilla Taskcluster
what_it_is: Mozilla's open-source, massive-scale task execution and CI framework powering Firefox and Gecko across cloud and hardware pools.
programmable_control: Start: `PUT /api/queue/v1/task/{taskId}` or `taskcluster api queue createTask`; Check: `GET /api/queue/v1/task/{taskId}/status` or `taskcluster task status <id>`; Stop: `POST /api/queue/v1/task/{taskId}/cancel` or `taskcluster task cancel <id>`. Official Go/JS/Python/Rust SDKs. Docs: https://docs.taskcluster.net/docs/reference/platform/queue/api
auth_method: Hawk-signed Taskcluster client credentials (`TASKCLUSTER_CLIENT_ID` / `TASKCLUSTER_ACCESS_TOKEN`) or `taskcluster signin`

pricing_model: Free and open source (MPL-2.0); self-hosted
os_platforms: Linux, Windows, macOS, Android hardware pools (Docker, Generic Worker, D2G)
fit_reason: Exceptionally well-designed Queue REST API + multi-language SDKs, though mainly used by Mozilla and massive OSS orgs.
